subject: general
question: Who is the highest law officer in a state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Advocate General**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Advocate General is the **highest law officer in a state**, as per Article 165 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• He/she is appointed by the **Governor of the State** and must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court.
 
• The Advocate General provides legal advice to the state government and represents the state in legal proceedings.
 
• He/she has the right to participate in proceedings of the state legislature but cannot vote.
 
• The office of the Advocate General is analogous to the Attorney General of India at the national level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Attorney General of India:**

 
 
• The Attorney General is the highest law officer at the national level, appointed by the President of India.
 
• He/she advises the Union Government and represents it in legal matters.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications for Advocate General:**
 
 
• Must be a citizen of India.
 
• Should have been an advocate for at least 10 years or a judicial officer for at least 10 years.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Advocate General:**
 
 
• Provides legal counsel to the state government on constitutional and legal matters.
 
• Represents the state in cases before the High Court and Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Advocate General and Attorney General:**
 
 
• The Advocate General operates at the state level, while the Attorney General operates at the national level.
 
• Both are responsible for legal advisories but differ in jurisdiction.
